recreation_prompt_markdown: Create a fast, single-screen arcade browser game called **Neon Hype Relay** set on a futuristic livestream concert stage. The player controls one glowing handheld microphone by dragging it with mouse or touch across the screen. Four stylized performers or callers are arranged in a 2x2 grid in the upper and middle stage area. During play, targets randomly become active and begin waiting for the mic; each has a visible patience ring that drains if ignored. When the microphone overlaps an active target, that target switches into a singing or live state and a progress ring fills while the mic remains on them. If the player keeps the mic there until the ring completes, award score, restore some hype, show a bright **“SYNC!”** style pop-up, spawn floating musical note particles, and flash a positive crowd-reaction image. If a waiting target times out, remove them, subtract a large chunk of hype, show a dramatic **“DROP!”** style message, and trigger a negative reaction cue. Also drain hype slowly over time so the player is always under pressure. End the run when hype reaches zero, then show a game-over card with the final relay score and a better end-state message for high scores. Present everything with a neon cyber-arcade aesthetic: dark purple-to-black gradients, cyan and pink glow lighting, glassy HUD panels, Orbitron-style techno typography, stage-light beams, a perspective floor grid, and punchy UI sound effects. The experience should feel like an endless score-chasing survival relay with increasing difficulty, where more targets can activate at once and patience windows get tighter the longer the run lasts.

identity.title: Neon Hype Relay
identity.premise: A neon arcade relay game where the player drags a shared microphone between waiting live-show callers or performers to keep the signal alive and the crowd energized.
identity.interaction_model: Real-time pointer or touch dragging on a fullscreen canvas; the player moves a microphone onto active targets and keeps it there until their performance meter fills.
identity.objective: Maintain the hype meter, prevent callers from timing out, and earn score by completing successful microphone handoffs before the live feed collapses.
identity.progression: The run begins with low pressure and gradually escalates as more callers can activate simultaneously, patience windows shrink, spawn pressure increases, and the player is pushed into longer survival-based score chasing.
identity.mood: Arcade-intense, flashy, reactive, and slightly chaotic with celebratory sync moments and dramatic failure drops.
likely_audience: players who enjoy score attack survival loops

Moderate confidence in the exact fiction: the active targets are named singers in code but framed as callers in UI copy, so the fantasy reads as a live performance relay rather than a literal singing simulator.
Moderate confidence that the game is best described as arcade survival coordination rather than a true rhythm game because timing to music is not mechanically enforced.

selected_top_5.reasoning: The game is an endless score-chasing survival loop with continuously increasing pressure, no fixed stage completion, and a fail state caused by sustained mistakes or depletion of a shared meter.

The entire fantasy is built around music performance, microphone handoffs, singers, musical notes, and audiovisual sync rewards, although the mechanics are routing/hover-based rather than beat-timing based.
The player rapidly routes a controlled object among a small set of discrete screen positions, creating a lane-selection feel even though free dragging replaces strict lane movement.
Active callers arrive as escalating timed threats that must be serviced before they damage the shared hype resource, which resembles defending against incoming waves through triage.
Success depends on fast reaction time, efficient movement, and maintaining pace under rising pressure, but the game is not a traversal platformer or obstacle course.
